description: Explanatory taxonomy for causes. Each cause declares exactly one category. Categories drive (a) report-grouping in the doctor view, (b) co-explanation grouping heuristics, (c) default narrative tone, and (d) downstream objective bias when the cause leads.

categories.label: Androgenic Causes
categories.description: Causes whose dominant driver is androgen signalling at the follicle, irrespective of upstream origin (genetic, PCOS-mediated, post-menopausal).

categories.label: Stress and Cycle-Timing Causes
categories.description: Causes whose dominant driver is acute or chronic perturbation of the hair-follicle cycle timing (HPA-axis, post-illness, postpartum, crash-diet).

categories.label: Nutritional Causes
categories.description: Causes whose dominant driver is substrate insufficiency — micronutrient or macronutrient gaps.

categories.label: Endocrine Causes
categories.description: Causes whose dominant driver is a named endocrine perturbation (thyroid, PCOS, peri/postmenopause).

categories.label: Metabolic Causes
categories.description: Causes whose dominant driver is insulin–glucose dysregulation or adiposity-related hormonal cross-talk.

categories.label: Autoimmune Causes
categories.description: Causes whose dominant driver is immune-mediated follicular targeting.

categories.label: Gut–Hair Axis Causes
categories.description: Causes whose dominant driver is absorption-side or microbiome-mediated insufficiency manifesting in hair.

categories.label: Scalp-Inflammatory Causes
categories.description: Causes whose dominant driver is perifollicular and surface scalp inflammation.

categories.label: Extrinsic / Structural Causes
categories.description: Causes whose dominant driver is shaft-level damage from environment, heat, or chemicals — not follicular dysfunction.

categories.label: Composite Causes
categories.description: Causes that are explicitly multi-driver and require a composite explanation. Reserved for multifactorial-hair-loss.

categoryRelationships.notes: Female AGA cases routinely co-lead with endocrine.
Scalp inflammation amplifies miniaturization but rarely leads when miniaturization is dominant.
Distinguishing patchy + AA-history from inflammatory dermatosis is a key disambiguation.
